title: Verify stored amount matches customer-facing display after currency conversion
gherkin:
Feature: Multi-currency conversion integrity
  Scenario: Customer-facing total matches persisted billing amount
    Given a transaction with amount 100.00 USD
    When the transaction is converted to EUR at rate 0.92
    Then the stored billing amount is 92.00 EUR
    And the customer-facing display shows 92.00 EUR
    And the stored amount equals the displayed amount
rationale: Core requirement that user-facing totals must always match persisted billing amounts exactly. This test validates the fundamental integrity constraint that prevents silent discrepancies between what is stored and what is shown to customers.

From: finance_director@toolchain.com
Date: 2026-03-03 11:00
Subject: Pilot concern about international billing presentation

Hi Team,

Finance has a concern related to the pilot rollout for internationally billed equipment.

For a subset of high-value inventory, we may need a billing presentation approach that works more cleanly across more than one currency context. The current specification covers general pricing and billing expectations, but it does not go into much detail about how pilot-specific currency presentation or conversion rules should be handled in customer-facing outputs.

Before any implementation shortcut is taken, please clarify whether currency conversion, display format, and invoice currency are supposed to be handled as strict accounting rules, temporary pilot behavior, or only a presentation-layer convention. We want to avoid a situation where the operational display becomes simpler, but the customer-visible totals no longer align cleanly with the underlying financial records.

Best,
Finance Dept.

title: Reject presentation simplification that creates financial mismatch
gherkin:
Feature: Multi-currency conversion integrity
  Scenario: Display-friendly simplification is rejected when it diverges from stored total
    Given a transaction with stored amount 92.47 EUR
    When a presentation layer attempts to simplify display to 92.50 EUR
    Then the system rejects the simplified display format
    And the customer-facing display remains 92.47 EUR
    And no financial discrepancy is introduced
rationale: Directly addresses the conflict that display-friendly simplification producing visible mismatches with stored totals should not be implemented. This ensures presentation concerns do not override accounting integrity.
usedContextItems: Display-friendly simplification in one layer that produces visible mismatches with stored totals should not be implemented
